summary: Riding Mountain National Park fire tower known from a 1972 newspaper item; no build date, design or site description found in the sources read.

facts.status_note: Not on the 2018 blog's list of five towers still standing in the park. No source read says what became of it.

events.note: A 1972 Brandon Sun item, quoted on the Canada Lookouts page, says a park fire warden worked at the Makinak tower. The year is the item's date, not a start or end of staffing.

evidence.supports: Makinak tower: a fire warden for Riding Mountain National Park worked there (1972 item)
evidence.quote: where he worked as a fire warden for the Riding Mountain National Park

evidence.supports: Forest fire lookouts were rare in national parks until the late 1930s; standard plan towers in the western parks
evidence.quote: Forest fire lookouts were rare in national parks until the late 1930s when the Dominion Forest service introduced a system of standard plan towers throughout the western parks.

evidence.supports: Around ten towers built in Riding Mountain National Park in 1938 and 1939
evidence.quote: Around ten towers were built in Riding Mountain National Park in 1938-1939.

evidence.supports: Exact count hard to determine; some towers built outside the park boundary
evidence.quote: The exact number is difficult to determine because some of these were built outside the park boundary

evidence.supports: General design: octagonal cabin eight feet across on a 40 or 50 foot steel tower
evidence.quote: Generally these lookouts were comprised of an octagonal cabin, eight feet in diameter, perched on top of a 40 or 50 foot steel tower.

evidence.supports: Only five towers remain in the park; Makinak is not among them
evidence.quote: Only five remain in the park: Baldy, Clear Lake (pictured here) and Sugarloaf, all built in 1938, and Heron Creek and Rolling River dating from 1949.

evidence.supports: The blog's park visit was in early August 2018
Lookouts largely phased out in the 1970s and many removed
evidence.quote: Fire lookouts were largely phased out in the 1970s and many of the lookouts were removed.

evidence.supports: Riding Mountain National Park is managed by Parks Canada
evidence.quote: Riding Mountain National Park is managed by the Parks Canada Agency

sources.title: The view from here: Fire Lookout Towers
sources.publisher: The view from here (blog by Jason Paul Sailer)

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only Makinak-specific source is the Canada Lookouts page, which quotes a 1972 Brandon Sun item; we did not read the newspaper itself. No build date, design, height, status or site description was found. The blog's 1938-39 build count does not name Makinak, so no build event is recorded. The brief's status and access were unknown; access is omitted because no source supports a level. The brief's coordinates were not checked. The firelookout.ca index loads by script and could not be read. Budget: three websearch.py calls and about eight page reads, over the per-tower limit, because the first searches found no Makinak-specific history.
